known_portal_bugs.area: Output Comparison verdict (render_output_compare + AI prompt + HTML report)
known_portal_bugs.symptom: Two completely DIFFERENT files reported PASS ('Perfect match', 0% score, 29 total / 0 matched / 0 in every bucket).
known_portal_bugs.cause: The verdict + display read report keys 'mismatches'/'missing_in_2'/'missing_in_1', but _oc_compare returns 'hard_diffs'/'only_in_1'/'only_in_2'. The wrong keys always came back empty → verdict ALWAYS PASS. The AI prompt and HTML 'Perfect match' banner also branched only on hard_diffs, ignoring disjoint/missing keys and the nothing-matched case.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.79: verdict now reads the real keys and FAILs on any hard_diffs OR only_in_1/only_in_2 OR (total>0 and matched==0) OR a parse error. AI confirmation prompt only fires on a genuine clean match. HTML banner + badge driven by the verdict. XML parse-error key is now content-hashed so two unparseable files can't falsely match.

known_portal_bugs.area: Template Compare / Generated input.json preview (Streamlit render)
known_portal_bugs.symptom: The completeness summary card showed RAW HTML as text — literal <div>/<span> tags and '✗ Data Map ID' pills — instead of rendering.
known_portal_bugs.cause: The HTML f-string passed to st.markdown(..., unsafe_allow_html=True) was indented to match Python code. Streamlit's CommonMark parser treats any line indented >=4 spaces as a code block, so the HTML rendered as literal text.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.80: build the card HTML as a single flat (un-indented) string; added _st_html() helper that dedents + strips per-line leading whitespace before st.markdown, and routed all 18 other indented-HTML blocks in the template-compare report through it.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: A single run took ~58 min (Biz Flow step alone ~32 min); no way to run multiple transactions at once; .env had to be mounted.
known_portal_bugs.cause: All flows ran sequentially on one browser; Dockerfile didn't bake credentials.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.89: (1) Dockerfile now bakes CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET/token URLs as build ARGs→ENV + writes a baked /app/.env. (2) run_profile_runner_batch_parallel runs N transactions concurrently, each in its own headless BrowserManager with an isolated profile dir (data/browser/parallel/worker-N), via a thread-local manager registry (_BROWSER_TLS) so the shared fill code targets the right browser. UI in the Profile Runner: 'Run multiple transactions in parallel' (1-3 workers). (3) Fast fill mode (sidebar toggle / FAST_FILL_MODE env) trims cosmetic settle waits via _fast_settle.
known_portal_bugs.perf_note: The 32-min Biz Flow is dominated by per-field strategy cascades hitting timeouts because BizFlow field IDs are randomized per session (dds-form-field-<random>), so raw-selector learning can't short-circuit across sessions. The real throughput lever is parallelism (run 2-3 flows at once), not shaving per-field waits. Fast mode helps modestly. Parallel runs MUST be headless; 2-3 workers is the safe ceiling per VM.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' when a flow has multiple transport profiles (configure_targets / target_transport_profile is a list).
known_portal_bugs.cause: Section accessors used `... or {}` which doesn't catch a list value.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.90: added _coerce_section_dict (returns first dict of a list, else {}) and applied it to all section accessors in Template Compare, the judge, canonical builder, Excel writer, and the config-manual flow_name/customer derivation.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Sidebar (App Controls, API Credentials, Fast mode) was not visible.

known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.90: main() now calls sidebar_controls() right after init_session(), wrapped in try/except so a sidebar error can't blank the page.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Deploy reported failure when the flow was actually already deployed (portal shows Edit/Undeploy instead of Deploy).
known_portal_bugs.cause: The deploy step only looked for a Deploy button.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.90: if Deploy isn't reachable but an Edit/Undeploy/Deployed marker is present on the row, treat as success.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: interface_type was free text; users didn't know the valid portal values.
known_portal_bugs.cause: No enumeration of the portal's Interface Type options.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.90: HIP_INTERFACE_TYPES constant + the editor renders interface_type as a dropdown (SFTP HAFT, SFTP Server, HTTPS, HTTPS-AS2, AS2, IBM MQ, Rabbit MQ, Kafka, NAS, S3), keeping any unknown extracted value selectable.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Sidebar background was dark blue while Streamlit's buttons/metrics rendered as white cards, so it looked broken (white-on-white text, floating white boxes).
known_portal_bugs.cause: hip_premium_ui_config CSS set the sidebar background to #152b45 (dark) with white text, but didn't restyle the default white button/metric surfaces.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.91: switched the sidebar to a light theme (#f7f9fc surface, dark #102033 text) matching the rest of the app, and explicitly styled sidebar buttons (white card, blue text), metrics, inputs, and expander headers for readability.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: No visual record of what the agent filled on each page.
known_portal_bugs.cause: Feature not present.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.92: capture a full-page screenshot after each task completes (both run paths), attach the path to the run entry, and show it inline in the task Details + a screenshots gallery. Best-effort — a screenshot failure never breaks the run.

known_portal_bugs.area: Profile Runner timing + screenshots + Learn tab
known_portal_bugs.symptom: No phase breakdown for slow steps; screenshots were a separate section; no way to learn from existing portal config.
known_portal_bugs.cause: Features not present.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.93: timing phase breakdown (portal load / agent think / fill), per-BizFlow-section screenshots shown in the task log under a collapsible (removed the separate gallery), and a Learn-from-portal button that crawls the portal and updates the KB.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Run Timing card leaked raw HTML (<div>/<span> shown as text) instead of rendering the per-task bars + phase breakdown.
known_portal_bugs.cause: v79.93 added a multi-line {_breakdown} HTML block inside an INDENTED triple-quoted f-string for bars_html and the card; Streamlit's CommonMark parser treats lines indented >=4 spaces as a code block, so the HTML rendered literally.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.94: rebuilt bars_html, the main Run Timing card, and the skill-update card as single flat (un-indented) strings. Verified the rendered card is one line with zero >=4-space-indented lines.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Breakdown showed agent think 0.0s, fill 0.0s, and a huge 'other' (e.g. 32m18s on Biz Flows) — uninformative.
known_portal_bugs.cause: v79.93 only wrapped a narrow LLM call + page nav; the actual field-fill work was never timed, so it all fell into 'other'. The agent fills deterministically (no LLM), so agent_think was ~0.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.95: compute phases as a clean decomposition — page_load + agent_think measured directly, fill = total task wall time − page_load − agent_think. Removed the 'other' line; relabeled to '⌨️ fill / form work'. Now 'fill' is the real number that explains slow steps.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Fast mode barely changed fill time (only 3 cosmetic sleeps were trimmed).
known_portal_bugs.cause: 172 per-field asyncio.sleep calls, only 3 routed through _fast_settle.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.95: routed 98 mid-range per-field settle sleeps (0.2–0.8s) through _fast_settle. With Fast mode ON these trim 60%, which can cut a ~32min Biz Flow fill toward ~21min. Short polling sleeps and long critical sleeps left untouched for reliability.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Deploy step showed Failed (red) even though the flow was already deployed and the portal showed Edit/View/Clone/Migrate.
known_portal_bugs.cause: The already-deployed (Edit) detection only ran AFTER two failed deploy-click attempts and searched too narrowly, so it often didn't fire → status 'partial'/failed.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.95: added an EARLY deployed-state check right after the row expands — if Edit (or View/Clone/Migrate, no Deploy) is visible, return success immediately → task status 'completed'.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Agent re-learned the same fields every run (re-ran the full id→label→placeholder cascade), so repeat runs were just as slow.
known_portal_bugs.cause: Session-stable cascade wins (label/placeholder/alias) set _selector_memory but were never persisted for cross-session replay; only replay-path wins were recorded.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.96: cascade wins on stable strategies now call _record_strategy_replay() → persisted to field_strategy_replay.json. _try_strategy_replay() runs first on every fill and replays the known-good strategy, skipping the cascade; falls back to learning only if the element isn't found. Repeat runs get progressively faster.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: No support for FTP transport profiles (only SFTP HAFT etc.).
known_portal_bugs.cause: FTP wasn't in the interface-type list, and a normalizer forced interface_type to SFTP HAFT, overriding any other value.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.96: added FTP to HIP_INTERFACE_TYPES; the normalizer now preserves valid types (FTP/SFTP Server/AS2/...) and only forces SFTP HAFT when blank or a stray AS2 leak. FTP flows through input.json + Excel + Profile Runner like SFTP HAFT.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Agent only knew SFTP-style fields; for HTTPS/HTTPS-AS2/IBM MQ/Kafka it didn't fill the type-specific fields (Protocol, HIP URL, Queue Manager, Kafka Provider, Grant Type, PSE Number, etc.).
known_portal_bugs.cause: No per-interface-type field schema.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.97: added HIP_INTERFACE_TYPE_FIELDS (full schema from portal screenshots) + _interface_fields_for() resolver (handles conditionals: OAuth2→grant_type, Apikey→pse_number, Kafka Cloudera→bootstrap_servers). The Profile Runner injects the selected type's fields into _stp_field_order so they fill in form order; the Input Builder editor shows only the relevant fields (with dropdowns for known options); FIELD label map updated so the fill engine finds them.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Agent's per-interface-type field knowledge depended on hardcoded screenshots; types without a screenshot weren't covered.
known_portal_bugs.cause: Learn-from-portal only scraped list rows + <select>; it didn't open the Create form or cycle interface types.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.98: added _deep_learn_transport_profile() — opens the Create form, cycles System Type × Interface Type, captures all fields + opens each dropdown for options + records links/notices, saves a live schema, and _interface_fields_for() prefers that learned schema. The agent now learns everything about the Transport Profile page itself.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Deep-learn opened the wrong Transport Profile link (/transportprofiles/create) and only covered Transport Profile; Document Types used /documenttypes (wrong).
known_portal_bugs.cause: Hardcoded URLs didn't match the authoritative default_profile_runner_page_urls map; the form is reached via list→Add, not a /create path.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.99: corrected all URLs (doctypes, datamaps, rules, transportprofiles, bizflows) and reach the form by opening the list page + clicking Add/Create. Added _deep_learn_all_portals() so the button deep-learns EVERY portal form, not just Transport Profile.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Deep-learn navigated to each page and waited but captured 0 fields — it wasn't actually opening the Create form (the '+ Add' button wasn't being clicked).
known_portal_bugs.cause: Deep-learn used a naive page.evaluate regex to find/click an Add button, which didn't match the portal's DDS '+ Add' control.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.100: added _dl_open_create_form() which reuses the EXACT proven Profile-Runner flow — inspect_page + list_interactives → _v28_agent_find_add_button → _v28_build_selector_for_item → _execute_action_with_target('click') → wait_for_overlay_inputs, with prepare_create_surface + CREATE_ACTION_TARGETS fallbacks. Both _deep_learn_transport_profile and _deep_learn_all_portals now use it, so the form actually opens and fields are captured.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Deep-learn only captured static fields; it didn't learn the inline '+ Add' controls that add/remove repeatable configuration attributes throughout the flow.
known_portal_bugs.cause: Capture only snapshotted the initial form.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.101: _dl_capture_repeatables() enumerates every inline add/remove control (excluding main Create/Submit/Cancel), clicks each add-control to reveal the repeatable row, and captures the delta fields — so the agent learns what can be added/removed (tags, conditions, actions, multiple TPs, steps) and each row's fields. Wired into the all-portals deep-learn and shown in the Learn tab.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Repeatable sections using icon-only controls (no text/aria-label) weren't detected.
known_portal_bugs.cause: Detection relied on text/aria/class matching.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.102: added unicode-glyph + SVG-href/class icon-hint detection AND a learn-by-effect fallback — click the icon and classify by whether form fields increase (Add) or decrease (Remove). Fully automatic; no need to be told which control.

known_portal_bugs.area: Learn — wizard depth + required flags + validation loop
known_portal_bugs.symptom: Deep-learn captured only the first step of multi-step wizards, didn't record required flags, and learning didn't feed back into the builder.
known_portal_bugs.cause: No wizard traversal, no required capture, no validator.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.103: _dl_walk_wizard walks all wizard steps (Biz Flow); snapshots capture required:true; _validate_against_learned_schema flags configs against the learned portal schema in the Input Builder editor.

known_portal_bugs.area: Input Builder + Profile Runner — multi-branch flows
known_portal_bugs.symptom: Editor only edited the FIRST dict of list sections (multi-branch flows: many target doc types/maps/TPs); HTTPS-AS2 schema lacked the real AS2 fields (AS2 IDs, certificates, MDN).
known_portal_bugs.cause: No list-aware editor; AS2 fields were placeholders pending a real case.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.104: _render_section_editor handles list sections — one editor per branch + add-branch button (in-place edits, unique widget keys per branch). HTTPS-AS2 schema replaced with the REAL field set from the AMAZON JAPAN case (partner/dell AS2 IDs, certificate + CN/expiry, dell AS2 URL, signing/encryption/MDN). Labels mapped so the Profile Runner fills them.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: source/target_transport_profile crashed after System Type: stp_section_error UnboundLocalError 'cannot access local variable _stp_field_order' — only 1 field filled.
known_portal_bugs.cause: v79.97 interface-field injection ASSIGNED to _stp_field_order inside the nested async fill function; Python then treats the name as local for the whole function, so the first read (before assignment) raises UnboundLocalError.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.105: build a separate local list (_stp_fields_iter = list(_stp_field_order)), insert interface fields into it, and iterate that — the closure name is never rebound.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Deep-learn showed Document Type 10, Data Map 1, Rule 1, Transport Profile 0, Biz Flow 0 fields.
known_portal_bugs.cause: The portal renders fields progressively as values are entered; an unfilled form has almost nothing to capture.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.105: learn from REAL runs — every run's field_intelligence is auto-merged into the learned schema after each task, and a '📥 Learn from completed runs' button does it on demand. Run UHAUL_POASN once and the schema fills with what the run actually saw.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Only the FIRST of multiple data maps/TPs/doc types was created; static single-task assumptions.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.106: normalization layer + list-aware add_task → one task per item with repeat_index. Both old and new input.json schemas supported.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: 'Create a Transport Profile' / 'create the Document Type' in chat failed — chat only explained, never executed.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.106: intent router detects creation/run intents and starts the Profile Runner via the proven state machine, using the cached plan or building one from the selected customer's input.json.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: AttributeError 'list' object has no attribute 'get' (repeated data_map) and TypeError list indices must be integers (repeated target TP) in _config_manual_to_input_json/_apply_direction_to_objects after the v79.108 parser returned lists.
known_portal_bugs.cause: Converter and direction-applier assumed dict sections.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.109: coerced representative reads + per-item direction application; lists preserved end-to-end. Proven by full-chain acceptance test T13.

known_portal_bugs.symptom: Second rule lost: generator produced 'Rule Configuration1' (openpyxl dedupe), parser only matched 'Rule Configuration( N)?'.

known_portal_bugs.area: BizFlow > Process Steps > Mapping Transformer sub-configuration
known_portal_bugs.symptom: UHAL-POASN live run filled 48/52: row 0 (Mapping Transformer) logged bf_step_sub_config_no_combos reason=sub-fieldset not found — its Document Type Version, Action, Target Document Type, and Rule(Version) combos were skipped. Enricher row worked.
known_portal_bugs.root_cause: Legend lookup used substring t.includes('mapping configuration') but the REAL portal legend is 'Mapping Transformer Configuration' (token in the middle) — never matches. Enricher matched only because its legend equals its keyword. Row 0 also raced the async render with no retry.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.124: token matching (legend must contain ALL of ['mapping','configuration'] / ['enricher','configuration']) in all three searches (row-scoped, doc-wide fallback, NEW post-wait retry ~0.9s 'retry_after_wait'). Locked by T108 truth table.
known_portal_bugs.expected_after_fix: BizFlow fill count 48 → 52 on the same UHAL input.

known_portal_bugs.area: Profile Runner > Rule Configuration > Configure Routing > condition rows > Attribute Name/Unit
known_portal_bugs.symptom: Live rule run: row 0 (Receiver) filled fully; row 1's Value=DELL filled but its Attribute Name/Unit=Sender never committed. Log showed cond_field_id_lookup found BOTH attr ids then rule_cond_section_error: TimeoutError with no attr_row1_result.
known_portal_bugs.root_cause: The whole condition-rows coroutine ran under manager._run(..., timeout=60). Row 0 settles + row-1 add-row poll timeout + the ~2.4s Attribute settle pushed past 60s, guillotining row 1's attribute select mid-flight. The per-row try/except never fired because the timeout was on the OUTER coroutine.
known_portal_bugs.fix: v79.136: (1) section budget 60→120s; (2) each per-row Attribute Name/Unit select wrapped in asyncio.wait_for(timeout=12) so it can't hang and always logs an outcome; (3) rows that fail to commit their attribute are tracked in _attr_pending and a POST-SECTION backfill re-fills them once all rows exist and the dialog is settled (attr_backfill_start/result). Locked by T199.
known_portal_bugs.expected_after_fix: Both condition rows' Attribute Name/Unit commit (Receiver + Sender); rule fill count includes the row-1 attribute.

direct_answers.what is the u-haul poack flow: U-HAUL POACK is XML-to-XML outbound. DellPOA enters via DELL_U-HAUL_POACK_SENDER_TP (AIC-DCE). Contivo (DELLCoPOACKXX02C) transforms it to PO_ACKNOWLEDGMENT XML. Delivered to dce-test-partner via U-HAUL_DELL_POACK_RECEIVER_TP.
direct_answers.what does transaction_root_element mean: TRANSACTION_ROOT_ELEMENT identifies a document by its XML root element tag. The portal shows only a Value field (no Expression). Enter just the root element name, e.g. DellPOA or PO_ACKNOWLEDGMENT. Never put an XPath in the Expression field for this type — the field does not exist.
direct_answers.when is expression shown for document id: Expression is shown only for ELEMENT_IN_PAYLOAD (XPath) and FILENAME. Hidden for TRANSACTION_ROOT_ELEMENT and PAYLOAD_CONTAINS. This applies to both document_identifier rows and attributes_to_configure rows.
direct_answers.what is uhi1001: UHI1001 is the U-HAUL organisation code used in the Contivo-produced PO_ACKNOWLEDGMENT XML target payload, in the ROUTING/@destination_value attribute. The source uses 'uhaul' as the partner identifier.
direct_answers.what is dellco01: DELLCO01 is the Dell organisation code used in the Contivo-produced PO_ACKNOWLEDGMENT XML, in ROUTING/@source_value and VENDOR/@vendor_id_number. The source DellPOA uses 'DELL ASN' as the From partner identifier.
direct_answers.what is a pass-through integration in hi: A pass-through integration in HIP means the document is routed from source to target with no transformation — no Contivo map, no Data Map object. Session 07 (2026-03-20) demonstrated this for ABNAMRO (B2BXML catalog outbound) and SUPERTRON (CSV inbound). The Biz Flow has no Mapping Transformer step — the Configure Target step routes directly to the target TP.
direct_answers.what is abnamro xml catalog doctype: ABNAMRO_XML_CATALOG_DOCTYPE: transaction_type=catalog-832, format=XML, version=1.0. Doc Identifier: TRANSACTION_ROOT_ELEMENT → B2BXML. Receiver attribute: ELEMENT_IN_PAYLOAD → /B2BXML/BuyerCatalog/CatalogHeader/Receiver. Observed in Session 07 (2026-03-20).
direct_answers.how does filename derived_from work: FILENAME derives an attribute value from the incoming document filename. Expressions: part[N] = Nth segment (0-indexed, default _ separator), part[N,D] = Nth segment with delimiter D, parts[N-M] = segments N through M joined, basename = filename without extension, extension = file extension. Example: Kohler_UK_Dell.csv → part[0]=Kohler, part[1]=UK, basename=Kohler_UK_Dell. Malformed or out-of-range expressions return null. Detailed in Session 09 (2026-04-24).
direct_answers.how do csv flat file expressions work in: CSV/flat-file expressions use ELEMENT_IN_PAYLOAD with these patterns: header:Name = named column 1st data row, header:Name.row[N] = named column Nth row, col[N] = column N (0-indexed) 1st data row, col[N].row[R] = column N row R, meta:col[N] = column N of the header/metadata row itself (not data row — e.g. meta:col[0]=CSV_PO is the transaction type). regex = first capture group of the regex pattern. Session 09 (2026-04-24) demonstrated with MICROCENTER POS, Kohler UK, BHC pipe files.
direct_answers.what is https-as2 interface type in hip: HTTPS-AS2 is a HIP Transport Profile interface type for AS2 protocol over HTTPS. Fields (Session 10, 2026-04-16): AS2 From ID, AS2 To ID, AS2 URL, MDN Type (Sync/Async/None), Signing Algorithm (SHA-256/SHA-1), Encryption Algorithm (AES-256/3DES), Content Type, Compression Required. SEW-Eurodrive AS2 IDs: AS2 From=AS2SEW, AS2 To=AS2SEW (confirmed from Session 06). AS2 test mailboxes: scgpluatap01.amer.dell.com:9090/imailweb/entry (UAT), b2bobizlinkmailbox.dell.com/imailweb/entry.
direct_answers.what are all 9 hip interface types: The 9 confirmed HIP interface types are: 1. HTTPS-AS2 (detailed in Session 10), 2. HTTPS, 3. IBM MQ (detailed in Session 07), 4. Kafka, 5. NAS, 6. Rabbit MQ, 7. S3, 8. SFTP HAFT (detailed in Session 02), 9. SFTP Server.
direct_answers.what map was used for staples 855: Staples 855 uses map DELLCo85541XE68C, class Transform_DELLCo85541XE68C, JAR Transform_DELLCo85541XE68C.jar, Contivo 6.7. Source: DellPOA (Custom XML), target: EDI X12 855. Trading Grid standard: Custom XML, doctype: POA, solution_id: DELL.COM.01. Confirmed in Session 08 (2026-04-09).
direct_answers.what derived_from does transaction type: Transaction Type attribute ALWAYS uses TRANSACTION_ROOT_ELEMENT as derived_from — in BOTH the source and target document types. The Config Manual XLSX may show ELEMENT_IN_PAYLOAD for Transaction Type, but the portal screenshot confirms TRANSACTION_ROOT_ELEMENT is correct. No Expression field is shown for this attribute. Observed on U-HAUL POACK source doc type (screenshot 2026-04-22 11:38 PM).
direct_answers.what is the map identifier pattern for x: Pattern: {ZARFileName}_{ClientName}. Example: DELLCo85541XE23C_DOUGLAS_STEWART. The ZARFileName is the map name from the JAR file (without Transform_ prefix). The ClientName is the partner/account name.
direct_answers.what is the source doc type name pattern: Pattern: FileType_Format_TransactionType_Version_IB. Example: XML_xCBL_PO_1.0_IB. IB = Inbound (source), OB = Outbound (target). Transaction type: EDIX12 PO=850, EDIFACT PO=ORDERS, CSV PO=CSV_PO, 855 POA=855.
direct_answers.what is the rule naming convention: Rule name pattern: {DataMapName}_{PartnerName}_RULE. Example: DELLCo85541XE23C_DOUGLAS_STEWART_RULE. Action name pattern: {DataMapName}_{PartnerName}_ROUTE. Mapping ID pattern: {DataMapName}_{PartnerName} (1.0).
direct_answers.what is the transport profile naming con: Pattern: {Protocol}_{PartnerName}_{Direction}. For SFTP-HAFT, use role-specific deployment groups: Sender/Dell/source = da-sender-sftphaft-dce-shared; Partner/Receiver/target = pt-receiver-sftphaft-dce-shared. For other interfaces, use the explicit input value or current live portal option; do not reuse the SFTP-HAFT defaults.
direct_answers.how to configure edi delimiters in hip: For X12 EDI target doc type: Data Element Separator = * (asterisk), Segment Separator = ~ (tilde). Example from EDI: ST*855*0001~ → * separates elements, ~ ends segment. These are entered in the Document Type configuration under EDI Delimiters.
direct_answers.where does the isa06 value come from in: ISA06 = Sender ID — copied from the 6th element of the ISA segment in the target EDI file. Example: ISA*00* *00* *14*128293714DBLP*ZZ*GHX* → ISA06=128293714DBLP. ISA08 = Receiver ID — 8th element. ISA15: T=Test, P=Production.
direct_answers.what is the routing rule name pattern in: Pattern: FLOWROUTE_{PartnerName}_{TxType}_ANS_XMLPOAR_OB. Example: FLOWROUTE_DOUGLAS_STEWART_PC_855_ANS_XMLPOAR_OB. Action name: same pattern + _ROUTE. Scope: LOCAL. Conditions: Receiver Equals {partner_id} AND Sender Equals DELL ASN.
direct_answers.what xpath to use for receiver in xml so: For DellPOA XML: /DellPOA/PurchaseOrderHeader/PartnerInformation/To/PartnerName for display name, or /DellPOA/PurchaseOrderHeader/PartnerInformation/To/PartnerIdentifier for the partner ID used in rules. Example value: DOUGLAS_STEWART (PartnerName) or DOUGLAS_STEWARTSPSDS (PartnerIdentifier).
direct_answers.what is the sender in an outbound hip fl: In an outbound flow, the Sender is ALWAYS Dell Premier (STATIC: DELL — always contains 'Dell'). The Receiver is the external trading partner (dynamic). Source: Agentic_SOP_O2C_Integration_Flow — locked rule.
direct_answers.what is the receiver in an inbound hip f: In an inbound flow, the Receiver is ALWAYS Dell Premier (STATIC — constant). The Sender is the external trading partner. Never use Buyer/Customer roles to determine direction. Source: Agentic_SOP_O2C_Integration_Flow.
direct_answers.how does the agent determine flow direct: From the O2C SOP: PO → Inbound (External → Dell). Order Acknowledgment, ASN, Invoice → Outbound (Dell → External). Use the XML root element to identify the transaction, then apply direction rule. Never use Buyer/Customer roles to infer direction.
direct_answers.what xpath pattern should the agent use: Always use absolute, header-level paths. Pattern: /<RootElement>/<Header>/<Entity>/<Field>. Examples: /PurchaseOrder/Header/PartnerInformation/From/PartnerName (Sender, inbound 850), /ShipmentNotice/Header/PartnerInformation/To/PartnerName (Receiver, outbound 856), /ShipmentNotice/Header/ShipmentNumber (Business Identifier, outbound 856). Paths must be absolute, single-value, header-level. Source: Agentic_SOP_O2C_Integration_Flow.
direct_answers.what are the stop conditions for the hip: Agent must STOP (no retries without correction) if: trading partner cannot be identified, transaction type is unknown, XML structure is invalid, platform-generated delimiters are overridden, BizFlow deployment fails, Business Identifier (BEG03 for 850) is missing, Receiver XPath does not resolve to exactly one value, multiple header-level partners found, direction is ambiguous, Sender is not STATIC:DELL for outbound. Source: Agentic_SOP_O2C_Integration_Flow.
direct_answers.can the agent override edi delimiters in: NO. HIP/Contivo generates all delimiters (segment, element, record) internally. The agent must accept platform-generated delimiters and never attempt to override them. Overriding causes errors. Known working example: WINONAHEALTH_XML_EDI_OB_FLOW. Source: Agentic_SOP_O2C_Integration_Flow.
direct_answers.what xml root element maps to which edi: OrderAcknowledgement → 855 (Order Acknowledgment). ShipmentNotice → 856 (Advance Ship Notice / ASN). Invoice → 810 (Invoice). PurchaseOrder → 850 (Purchase Order). Source: Agentic_SOP_O2C_Integration_Flow.
direct_answers.what is the business identifier for each: 850 PO inbound: BEG03 (Purchase Order Number) from EDI → /PurchaseOrder/Header/PurchaseOrderNumber in XML. 855 ACK outbound: /OrderAcknowledgement/Header/OrderNumber → BAK03 in EDI. 856 ASN outbound: /ShipmentNotice/Header/ShipmentNumber → BSN02 in EDI. 810 Invoice outbound: /Invoice/Header/InvoiceNumber → BIG04/IT1 in EDI. Source: Agentic_SOP_O2C_Integration_Flow.
direct_answers.what is the douglas stewart map name: Map Name: DELLCo85541XE23C. Map Class: Transform_DELLCo85541XE23C. Map Identifier: DELLCo85541XE23C_DOUGLAS_STEWART. JAR: Transform_DELLCo85541XE23C.jar. XBM: DELLCo85541XE23C.xbm. Contivo Version: 13.3 (not 6.7 — version is map-specific).
direct_answers.what is the douglas stewart partner id: DOUGLAS_STEWARTSPSDS — used in Rule conditions (Receiver Equals DOUGLAS_STEWARTSPSDS) and Document Identifier ELEMENT_IN_PAYLOAD → /DellPOA/PurchaseOrderHeader/PartnerInformation/To/PartnerIdentifier = DOUGLAS_STEWARTSPSDS. Sender = DELL ASN.
direct_answers.what are the isa segment values for doug: ISA06=114315195INOVP (Sender), ISA08=DOUGLASSTEWART (Receiver), ISA05=14, ISA07=ZZ, ISA12=00401, ISA15=P (Production), ISA16=>. GS02=114315195INOVP, GS03=DOUGLASSTEWART, GS08=004010. REF*IA*3135 = Internal Vendor Number (used as PAYLOAD_CONTAINS REF*02=3135).
direct_answers.what is the contivo version for douglas: Contivo Version 13.3 for DELLCo85541XE23C (Douglas Stewart 855 outbound). Note: Contivo version is map-specific — not all maps use 6.7. Always check the Configuration Manual for the correct version per integration.
direct_answers.what type of transport profile does doug: Douglas Stewart target TP uses SFTP Server (not SFTP HAFT). Server: sftpbizp11.tgms.gxs.com, Port 22, Path /send, Auth: Password.
